ai.description: *Raorchestes theuerkaufi* is a small shrub frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct yellow-spotted flanks. It features a prominent white sub-tympanic spot and translucent, yellowish belly skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes theuerkaufi* is best distinguished by its unique, vibrant reddish-brown iris, which contrasts sharply with the eyes of other similar bush frogs in the region.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes theuerkaufi* is endemic to the Western Ghats, typically inhabiting the leaf litter and low-lying vegetation of evergreen rainforests at mid-to-high altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes theuerkaufi* is a nocturnal shrub frog that remains active at night, primarily foraging for small insects among the foliage of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes theuerkaufi* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of terrestrial eggs, with breeding occurring during the monsoon.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes theuerkaufi* is endemic to the central Western Ghats in the Indian state of Karnataka, specifically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes theuerkaufi* is a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted by males from within dense evergreen forest canopy.
